web_sources.says: ST user manual UM2884 for the VL53L5CX driver. Table 2, minimum and maximum ranging frequencies: 4x4 1 to 60 Hz, 8x8 1 to 15 Hz; the default is 1 Hz; the resolution is set before the frequency. Continuous mode keeps the emitter on, so range and ambient immunity are better; autonomous mode is the default and takes an integration time. Changing the resolution also changes the I2C traffic when results are read.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026; the vendor's site could not be opened directly from this session

web_sources.says: ST VL53L5CX datasheet, DS13754 (distributors' copies). I2C at 400 kHz to 1 MHz, address 0x52; up to 400 cm ranging; the integration time applies in autonomous mode only; the detection volume depends on reflectance, ambient light, resolution, sharpener, ranging mode and integration time. Field of view: revision 2 says 63 deg diagonal; revision 13 lists 45 deg horizontal, 45 deg vertical and 65 deg diagonal. The field of view is measured with a white 88 % target square to the sensor at 1 m, in the dark, at 8x8.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026; the maximum-range tables (17 and 18) were not in any extract, and the file hosts could not be opened directly

web_sources.says: ST application note AN5894 on the fields of view of its ToF sensors: for the VL53L5CX the field is given on the diagonal (65 deg) and by side (45 x 45 deg), and the side cannot be converted to the diagonal with Pythagoras' theorem.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026

web_sources.says: An ST community question on how to read 'typical' and 'minimum' in the VL53L5CX datasheet's tables 17 and 18 of maximum range capability (table 18 is on page 20). It shows that the tables exist; it gives no value, and the extract held no answer.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026; used only to name the tables that were not read

web_sources.says: An ST presentation of October 2023 lists the VL53L5CX at 400 cm in the dark and 170 cm in ambient light, with no target, resolution or rate beside the figures.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026

web_sources.says: Pololu's page for its VL53L8CX carrier: in 5000 lux the VL53L8CX is expected to detect a large reflective target out to about 2.8 m, against about 1.7 m for the VL53L5CX; the 4 m maximum of both assumes an ideal dark environment; effective range and update rate depend on the configuration, the target and the environment. No resolution or rate is given with the 1.7 m.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026; the catalog note on pololu_vl53l8cx cites the same page

web_sources.says: A copy of an ST guide for the VL53L5CX, which the search tool names UM2887 revision 1, the software integration guide. Its table of I2C bandwidth during ranging lists packet sizes of 124, 316, 1008 and 3360 bytes and bandwidths of 124, 316, 63000 and 50909 bytes per second. Three rows were read with their configuration: 1 Hz, 4x4, one target per zone, distance, target status and number of targets only: 124 bytes; 60 Hz, 4x4, four targets per zone, all output enabled: 1008 bytes, 63000 bytes per second; 15 Hz, 8x8, four targets per zone, all output enabled: 3360 bytes, 50909 bytes per second. The 316-byte row did not come back with its configuration.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026; the 316-byte row is taken to be the 124-byte row's outputs at 8x8, which is this document's reading (d)

web_sources.says: ST user manual UM3109 for the VL53L8CX (the catalog's newer part, pololu_vl53l8cx): the same limits, 4x4 1 to 60 Hz and 8x8 1 to 15 Hz.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026

web_sources.says: ST community answers by an ST employee: several VL53L5CX sensors interfere a little (an extra target with an invalid status); ST tested sensors set at different angles and found the effect minimal. Forum answers, not a specification.
web_sources.read_how: through the web search tool's extract on 14 Nov 2026; used only as a note, kind (d)

rt_core.label: 2. Isolated real-time core on the Jetson reads the ToF pair and stops
rt_core.design: the alternative the delay bench test measures (P30); PR #668 (unverified) calls it Partial PLEM
